messages.author: de3190e0e6f4a690
messages.subject: Plotting fit$marginals.fixed effects
parts:
Hi all,

I'm following up on a previous topic about plotting covariate effects from inla (in this case inlabru).
I'm trying to plot the marginals.fixed from my model, with the 0.05 & 0.975 CI on either side and mean in the middle, as shown here.
https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/113940/in-r-and-inla-how-do-i-graph-results-of-rw2-model

I think my hang up is that I I think the 'ID' object here refers to the locations of the predictions, and I don't know what the equivalent of that would be in my model.

I have 8 fixed effects in my model, and if I could present them this way it be really handy in terms of explaining how the predicted density of my predictions relates to values from these continuous spatial covariates.

###
PS- for a separate graph, I'm trying to plot the variables together to show their relative 'significance' using ggregplot, but can't get a version of package to load in r.
Has anyone used this package/ found an old repository version that works?
https://ourcodingclub.github.io/tutorials/inla/

Thanks for your help & feedback.

Cheers,
Sol

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: Plotting fit$marginals.fixed effects
parts:
Hi Sol,

If you are using inlabru, then plotting predictions of fixed effects is pretty straight forward. See instructions from Thierry Onkelinx here: https://www.muscardinus.be/2018/07/inlabru-bru/.

Best, 
Tim
